label: sim-phones-strong-1
assignment: Should Phones Be Allowed in Class?
source: simulated demo student (persona: strong) run through the real platform
content: I am against allowing phones in university classes. First, phones distract both the user and classmates, breaking the flow of learning. Second, phones can be a tool for cheating; students might copy answers or look up solutions during exams. In my first semester, we had a group presentation on data science. One teammate kept checking his phone for a quiz app, which slowed our rehearsal and caused us to miss key points. We ended up losing marks for incomplete content. An objection might be that phones help students access quick references. However, we can use printed notes or approved devices during exams, ensuring academic integrity while still benefiting from instant information.

questions.answer: Mera matlab yeh tha ke jab koi student class mein phone use karta hai, to woh sirf khud ko hi nahi balki uske classmates ko bhi distract karta hai. Phone ka light, notifications aur apps ki tez cheezein sabki attention ko tod deti hain, jis se lecture ka flow break ho jata hai aur sab ko samajh mein mushkil hoti hai. Yeh sach hai kyun ke research se pata chalta hai ke mobile use se concentration levels kam hote hain aur students ki performance pe negative impact padta hai.

questions.prompt: You wrote, "phones distract both the user and classmates, breaking the flow of learning." What did you mean by this, and why do you consider it to be true?

questions.answer: Even if phones are only allowed for quick notes, students still tend to glance at social media or other apps in the background, so distraction remains. The mere presence of the phone makes it easy to switch topics, which breaks the lecture flow.
questions.feedback: You correctly applied your distraction argument to a scenario where phones are allowed only for note‑taking.
questions.prompt: If a professor allows phones only for taking quick notes during a lecture, how would your main argument about phones being a distraction still apply?
